Class PreMatchChecks

java.lang.Object
frc.spectrumLib.checks.PreMatchChecks
public final class PreMatchChecks extends Object
Pre-match self-checks: a registry of Checks that run while the robot is disabled and add up to one GO / NO-GO.

Each check gives PASS, WARN, FAIL or SKIP with a one-line reason. The robot is NO-GO while any check fails; warnings are shown but do not change GO. Results are outputs, never inputs to anything: the checks are advisory and never stop the robot from enabling.

Outputs, under the prefix given (e.g. PreMatch):

  • Go and Reason: the verdict and one line saying why, on NetworkTables for Elastic and the pit app.
  • Summary: one line per check, "FAIL CAN: ...", on NetworkTables too.
  • Checks/<name>/Status and Checks/<name>/Reason.
  • Active: whether the checks are running (disabled, before a match starts). While not, the last results stay published but nothing is re-judged.

A failing check raises a HIGH alert and a warning a MEDIUM one, both cleared on enable: in a match the subsystems' own alerts speak for themselves. Once a match has started (the first enable with the FMS attached), the checks stay quiet until the FMS detaches, so the disabled gap between auto and teleop raises nothing; the pre-match results stay published as they were.

One check is evaluated per loop, in turn, so the cost is one check's work whatever the number registered. Every check's Check.observe(double) still runs every loop.
